title: Landing a finished loop is still a manual step
tier_reason: The animation prompt tells each parallel run not to commit, because they share one working tree.
ask: The animation prompt tells each parallel run not to commit, because they share one working tree. That is right, but it leaves a person to land every finished loop by hand, which is the shape of defect Daniel's own doctrine names: a recurring manual step is not a process. Work out how a finished loop reaches main without anybody remembering to do it — a drain pass that picks up completed out/ directories and their scripts, or the runs committing to their own branches.
first_action: Decide how a finished loop lands on main without a human step, and write it up against whichever lane already does the closest thing
source_message: Filed 2026-09-08 when Daniel asked whether there is now a system for adding animations to the Design Studio's animation page. The answer was most of one; these are the places it is not closed.
result: The requested process design is on origin/main at a7b27a8 in docs/hq/ANIMATION_LANDING_PLAN.md. It specifies a durable finished-run receipt, the scheduled drain as collector, exact captured source/render/showcase files, exported game sheet and manifest, validation, same-path conflict holds, candidate rebuilding when main changes, replay-safe local commit and fast-forward push, and recovery after failures. The animation prompt now states honestly that landing remains manual. Focused Animation Lab tests passed (13/13), git diff --check passed, and the writing gate found no new concerns. GitHub CI was in progress when checked. This closes the design ask only; the receipt collector and automatic push are not implemented.
